_readme: BSI Customizer sign-in configuration template - the only version of this file
that is committed. Copy it to auth.json next to the EXE (or anywhere and point
BSIC_AUTH_FILE at it) and fill that in; never commit or ship the filled-in copy.
Every value here can come from an environment variable instead - see _env below.
Access is granted when EITHER gate passes:
1. discord.allowUsers lists the Discord user ID, OR
2. discord.guildId + discord.roles + discord.requiredTier: the signed-in user
is a member of that server and holds a listed role whose tier matches.
The role gate uses GET /users/@me/guilds/{guildId}/member, which needs the
guilds.members.read scope (added automatically when a role gate is configured,
so the identify-only scope below is enough).
discord.clientSecret is OPTIONAL: the app is a public OAuth2 client using PKCE.
If Discord answers invalid_client with an empty secret, either enable the Public
Client flag for the application (Developer Portal -> OAuth2) or set the secret.
The whole file can also be baked into the build from the ZLP_AUTH_JSON secret
(or passed as the ZLP_AUTH_JSON env blob) - see _embed below.

discord_portal: Add a redirect URI in the Discord developer portal that matches exactly:
Scheme, host, port and path all have to match, and 127.0.0.1 is used
instead of localhost on purpose (localhost may resolve to ::1).
_embed: ZLP_AUTH_JSON (repository secret) = this whole auth.json as one blob,
embedded into the EXE at build time by the GitHub Actions workflows.
ZLP_AUTH_JSON as a runtime env var (alias BSIC_AUTH_JSON) supplies the
same blob and wins over any file. Precedence: per-field BSIC_DISCORD_*
env vars > ZLP_AUTH_JSON blob > BSIC_AUTH_FILE > auth.json next to the
EXE > auth.json in app data > the build-time embedded blob.
